label: qwen
run_context: Owner-approved RE-RUN (2026-08-21, superseding the original run cut by the previous pod's spend hard stop -- see _invalid-cut-20260821/raptor/qwen-hardstop/ for that discarded partial run, kept for the record only). This run used pod-qwen-medium (medium effort) on a fresh, speed-tuned 2xH200 pod at the model's native 262,144 context, harness window matched. Same 6 scripted turns as the original plan, per-turn runaway guard raised to 6h (never triggered -- see per-turn wall times below; DeepSeek never exceeded 25 min/turn either, so the wider guard cannot have affected its result). All 6 turns completed naturally with rc=0; turn 3 (the M3 milestone turn) spanned a pod/server outage mid-turn -- its transcript (turn-3.json) contains 27 HTTP 502 and 53 HTTP 503 responses, consistent with the harness retrying through an outage rather than the model working continuously; that turn's wall time (8382s) is NOT a real measure of model working time and is disclosed as such wherever it's reported below.

milestones.label: renders level + ship
milestones.notes: SSIM 0.2373 (bar 0.80) and palette_coverage 0.069 (bar 0.90), both well below DSV4's own M1 fail (0.494/0.862). Captured twice from independent fresh page loads (byte-identical both times -- window.__raptor.ready deterministic capture point: player alive at (160,176), hud.score=10000, hud.shields=100, wave=1, 2 enemies tracked -- so the GAME STATE at capture is fully populated and correct). The rendered canvas itself (captured via canvas.toDataURL(), the raw committed pixel buffer, not a page screenshot -- so this is not a CSS-scaling or capture-timing artifact) shows a horizontal banding defect: alternating scanline bands of plausible terrain color and near-black, on top of what also looks like a more terrain-heavy / less-ocean scroll position than the reference frame (expected per the pre-disclosed M1 frame-timing limitation, see LIMITATIONS.md -- but the banding itself is not explained by that limitation). Not root-caused in depth (the scorer does not edit or debug model code); a grep of js/game.mjs's pixel-buffer writes (`px[row+...]`-style per-pixel/per-row loops used for terrain/sprite blitting and a few color-remap-table applications) is consistent with, but does not confirm, a per-scanline blit/stride defect in the terrain draw path -- offered as a lead, not a diagnosis.

milestones.label: arrow keys move ship, fire spawns projectile
milestones.notes: player moved (x 160->220 under sustained ArrowRight), fire produced 4 live projectiles.

milestones.label: wave-1 enemies, hit decrements HP / removes enemy, player can die
milestones.notes: best-effort coarse-aim hit test (checker's own documented caveat, same caveat applied to DSV4's passing M3 result): target enemy HP stayed 7->7 (no decrement), enemy not removed; player alive flag reported correctly. time_to_s (8382s / 2h19m42s) spans the pod/server outage described in run_context above (27x HTTP 502 + 53x HTTP 503 in this turn's transcript) -- NOT a measure of real model working time; disclosed here rather than adjusted, since the actual productive-work fraction of this turn cannot be reliably separated from the outage/retry fraction after the fact.

milestones.label: HUD renders; Web Audio running, >=1 SFX on fire
milestones.notes: Not independently attempted -- the shared m2_m5_playwright.mjs checker gates M4 on M3 passing ("skipped: M3 did not pass"), identical gating logic applied to both models' runs (would equally have skipped DSV4's M4 had ITS M3 failed). time_to_s (624s) is the model's own M4 milestone-turn duration; the model's own build does implement HUD/audio (window.__raptor.hud/audio fields are present with correct shape at every capture), but this was never independently verified against the acceptance check because the ladder never reached it.

milestones.label: sector-1 loop: wave counter to 9 + sector-complete screen
milestones.notes: Dedicated 3x procedure (pre-committed pass-if-any rule, same procedure and same 600s cap used for DSV4): 0/3 passed. Attempt 1: final_wave=1, sector_complete=false, died=false, elapsed_s=600.02 (timed out). Attempt 2: final_wave=1, sector_complete=false, died=false, elapsed_s=600.04 (timed out). Attempt 3: final_wave=1, sector_complete=false, died=false, elapsed_s=600.08 (timed out). Notably different failure mode from DSV4 (which died at wave 1 in ~100s all 3 attempts): here the state-aware dodge survives the full 10-minute cap every time without dying, but the wave counter never advances past 1 -- plausibly related to the port's own documented "training difficulty" tuning (full shield refill per wave, 2.4s i-frames after every hit, hazard-zone damage scaling; see the port's own README.md "Difficulty / accessibility tuning" section, unmodified by this packaging/scoring step) making the checker's dodge policy effectively unkillable but not exercising whatever advances the wave counter. DISCLOSURE: the model's own commit message (be941fe) and its own test/smoke.mjs report a full natural sector clear (waves 1-9, sector-complete screen) under the model's OWN autoplay driver -- a materially different result from the shared checker's state-aware dodge here. Per SCORING.md §6 (no editing briefs/checkers between models) and the pre-committed M5 procedure, the SHARED checker's result is what is scored; the model's self-reported pass is disclosed, not adopted, and not root-caused further (would require debugging why this build's wave-advance condition and the checker's contract-only dodge don't interact the same way the model's own driver does).

Architecture note: unlike the discarded original run (which pre-baked GLB data into a 32k-line generated js/assets.js at build time), this build fetches the two shareware GLB archives at runtime via fetch() -- the same architecture DSV4 uses -- so no generated-assets exclusion note is needed for the private repo (data/*.GLB is covered by the existing .gitignore, same as DSV4).

compaction.method: grep count of 'compaction_start' events in each turn-N.json -- raptor_secondary_metrics.py itself does not compute compaction counts (checked: no compaction logic in the script), so this is added manually, same underlying event data OMP's own compaction audit used elsewhere in this study.
compaction.note: Far fewer compaction cycles than the discarded 131k-capped attempt from the ORIGINAL (superseded) run saw in a comparable window (21+ cycles there vs 8 here across the whole session), consistent with the native 262144 context window reducing but not eliminating compaction pressure -- the opening (general-exploration) turn still triggered 6 cycles even at 262k. Turn 3's single compaction coincides with that turn's pod-outage window (see run_context/M3 notes) but is not necessarily caused by it -- turn 3 was also the longest-running milestone turn by far, which alone would raise compaction odds.
